Trailing semiconductor nodes are filling at greater rates, leading-edge nodes fully allocated with ~1-year lead times. Dell is 'repricing every day' in the inflationary environment, and customers are signing 3-5 year multiyear supply agreements to secure access. Year-over-year, each server carries MORE cores, MORE DRAM and MORE NAND (content growth on top of unit growth).

Around it, the Dell IP storage portfolio is explicitly described as the company's margin lever (commercial PCs and traditional servers are run for sustained, not rising, margin rate): PowerStore was the 10th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth in Q2, PowerScale now 5 quarters in a row of growth and ObjectScale 4 quarters in a row, all at higher ASPs because of the attached software and services.

Dell has LTAs and capacity agreements in place with its memory partners, repriced its entire server business on December 10 and tens of thousands of open PC quotes on January 6, is moving to discount-off-list pricing with the shortest quote validity ever, and names securing supply as the first priority. The FY2027 AI guide is bounded partly by 'the availability of DRAM and E1 drives and E3 drives'.

DRAM and NAND now account for almost 56% of total BOM cost on a low-end smartphone, forcing OEMs to trim specifications; smartphone units are still expected down 10-15% in 2026. NAND makers are redirecting focus and CapEx to DRAM and HBM, deemphasising eMMC/UFS and exiting automotive - which hands share to Silicon Motion's module-maker customers and gives it stronger pricing power. These are controller-plus-NAND solutions, so ASPs are much higher than controller-only (and higher than MonTitan). The DRAM-less boot drive is the crown jewel: conventional DRAM-based boot drives for server CPUs stay with the NAND makers, but DPUs, TPUs, NPUs and switches favour DRAM-less designs for cost, security and performance - and NAND makers have no DRAM-less PCIe SSD controllers and little incentive to build them for a market where densities are only 256GB-512GB. A server rack can carry more than 30 or 40 boot drives, and per-drive capacity should rise. Management sees little competition from either NAND makers or module makers, and said Ferri plus Boot Drive reaching roughly one third of revenue in 2027 is 'certainly a possibility' given current backlog and pipeline.

Training creates the initial data foundation, inference generates data continuously, agentic systems multiply the volume and frequency, and physical AI accelerates the cycle further - so storage demand shifts from a one-time infrastructure build to the ongoing compounding of retained data. The largest AI platforms now process TENS OF BILLIONS OF TOKENS PER MINUTE and BILLIONS OF PROMPTS PER DAY with token volumes growing severalfold YoY. Roughly 80% OF DATA STORED IN A HYPERSCALE DATA CENTER SITS ON HARD DISK DRIVES, and management expects that to hold. For PHYSICAL AI (autonomous vehicles, robotics, humanoids, industrial automation) real-world data is INSUFFICIENT to train the models, so operators generate and must store SYNTHETIC DATA SETS for reinforcement learning - a new demand vector. On inference specifically: storing generated context is MORE ECONOMICAL THAN RE-RUNNING IT through compute and memory. Core cloud services (notably stored video/collaboration recordings) remain an underappreciated parallel driver, and cheaper open-source Asian models are viewed as demand-positive since more model access means more data

Now we're starting to see more what I'll call object stores. Where what's really happening at layers above us, in memory layers, say, is that you are having very fast transactions on metadata, then when you need that specific data underneath, you pull it up.
